magic_items.name: Penbregol
magic_items.description: Penbregol is a Woodland Bow (see page 159 of the Player's Guide) with the Superior Keen enchanted quality (see the Loremaster's Guide, page 138). The magical bow is irreplaceable and is traditionally held by the captain of the Elvenking's guard. Any mortal who chooses to keep the bow is regarded with Mistrust by any Elves, who recognise it on sight.

magic_items.name: The Roadwarden's Staff
magic_items.description:
The magnificent staff of the roadwarden is a walking stick of Dwarf-make, with a shaft of polished wood topped with a pearl as great as a small dove's egg. Its maker engraved runes of power and protection on the wooden shaft. A hidden compartment inside the staff once contained maps of the Old Forest road, but Bofri does not know if they are still intact.

The staff might be worth up to 20 gold pieces, maybe much more if sold to Dwarves. It also has three special benefits:
• The bearer of the staff has a +1 modifier to Embarkation and Arrival rolls (in addition to any other modifiers).
• Certain doors, supply caches and vaults associated with the Old Dwarf Road only open for the bearer of the staff.
• A Dwarf who bears the staff and is acknowledged as the Warden of the Road has Advantage on all audiences with other Dwarves.

magic_items.name: Great War-horn of the Hunter
magic_items.description: Fashioned of old from the horn of one of the great kine of Araw by a Gondorian hero by the name of Vorondil, it was given to a prince of Rhovanion as a gift (Vorondil wore its mate on a baldric, and the horn is today an heirloom of his family, the House of the Stewards of Gondor). The Great War-horn of the Hunter may be blown as an action in combat. All allies of the war-leader may then use their reaction to recover hit points equal to 7 (2d6) plus the war-leader's Proficiency Bonus. Once the Great War-horn has been sounded, the war-leader must take a short rest before using it again.

magic_items.name: The Torc of Fram
magic_items.description: A treasure of the ancestors of Rohan, this torc of gold with garnets was looted from the ruins of a town in the Vales of Gundabad where that folk dwelt for a time. The torc gives anyone who wears it the Lordly Distinctive Quality.

magic_items.name: The Cup of Kinship
magic_items.description: Another treasure from the Vales of Anduin, it is said that those who drink from this golden cup are forever bound together in true friendship. If everyone in the Company drinks from the cup, then the first time in an Adventuring phase that any hero gains Inspiration, everyone in the Company gains Inspiration. This bond can be renewed once every year.

equipment.name: Weighted Net
properties: immunity to bludgeoning, poison and psychic damage

features.name: Ambush
features.description: During his first turn, the Servant has Advantage on attack rolls against any creature that hasn't taken a turn.

features.name: Craven
features.description: If the Servant starts his turn with 9 or less hit points, he must make a DC 10 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, he becomes Frightened and must use his Dash or Disengage action to move away from any enemies. If movement is impossible, he will take the Dodge action instead.

actions.name: Broadsword
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 5 (1d8+1) slashing damage.

features.name: Hunter
features.description: The Savage Hound doubles its Proficiency Bonus for all Wisdom (Perception) checks (included above).

features.name: Pack Tactics
features.description: The hound has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the its allies is within 5 feet of the creature and that ally isn't Incapacitated.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +4 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 5 (1d6+2) piercing damage.

features.name: Sunlight Curse
features.description: Stone-trolls become Petrified and turn into stone if they are touched by the bright light of the sun. If exposed to sunlight, the Stone-troll chief must make a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw at the beginning of its turn in order to find enough cover to avoid being turned to stone. On a failure, the Stone-troll becomes Petrified.

actions.name: Clobbering Sweep (1/day)
actions.description: The Stone-troll Chief can use his great size to strike multiple foes at once. He can make a melee attack against any number of targets within 5 feet, with a separate attack roll for each target. Targets must also make a DC 13 Dexterity check or be knocked Prone.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The Stone-troll chief makes three attacks: two with his troll-club and one slam.

actions.name: Troll-club
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 13 (2d8+4) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Slam
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 15 (2d10+4) bludgeoning damage.

features.name: Fear of Fire
features.description: If a torch or other flame comes within 10 feet of him, Raegenhere suffers Disadvantage on his attack rolls.

features.name: Savage Assault
features.description: When Raegenhere rolls a natural 18 or 19, he may, as a bonus action, make a single additional melee attack against the same opponent.

features.name: Thing of Terror (1/day)
features.description: Raegenhere is an evil spirit wearing a living man like a suit of armour. He briefly shows his true form and each hero must make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or be Frightened of him until the end of his next turn.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Raegenhere can make two attacks; one with his axe and one with his claws.

actions.name: Great Axe
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 9 (1d12+3) slashing damage.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 6 (1d6+3) slashing damage.

reactions.name: Fell Spirit (Recharge 5-6)
reactions.description: When Raegenhere would be reduced to 0 hit points, he may use his reaction to add 10 (3d6) temporary hit points.

monsters.name: The Forest Dragon
languages: Unknown (no one in this Age of the world has heard her speak)

features.name: Deadly Tail-grip
features.description: The Forest Dragon has one Legendary action each turn, which she can use to cause 13 (1d12+7) bludgeoning damage to a Grappled foe.

features.name: Mirkwood Dweller
features.description: If the Forest Dragon is within 5 feet of a Mirkwood scenery feature, she may use her bonus action to gain half-cover from it, even if the feature would not normally provide it.

features.name: Thing of Terror
features.description: The Forest Dragon can use her bonus action to rear up and display her full strength. Each hero within 60 feet must make a DC 19 Wisdom saving throw or be Frightened of her until the end of her next turn.

features.name: Tough Hide
features.description: The Forest Dragon is resistant to non-magical bludgeoning and slashing damage.

features.name: Weak Spot
features.description: If the Forest Dragon uses a special ability that uses an action (Crushing Tail-grip or Multiattack), any heroes that are within range may use their reaction to make a single attack. For this attack only, she is considered vulnerable to all piercing, slashing and bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: The Forest Dragon makes two Bite attacks.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +11 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 20 (3d8+7) piercing damage.

actions.name: Crushing Tail-grip
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +11 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 13 (1d12+7) bludgeoning damage. The target becomes Grappled (escape DC 21). The dragon can spend its action to cause 13 (1d12+7) bludgeoning damage to the Grappled foe.

features.name: Echolocation
features.description: Valdis cannot use her blindsight while Deafened.

features.name: Enthrall
features.description: As a bonus action, Valdis (in her illusionary form) can force a creature within 60 ft to make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or become Charmed by her. A Miserable Charmed creature gains the Thrall ability, see The Thrall Curse, opposite page. The Charmed effect lasts until Valdis leaves the area, attacks the Charmed creature, or the creature takes a short rest.

features.name: Keen Hearing
features.description: Valdis has Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing.

features.name: Fell Speed
features.description: Valdis may take a bonus action to Disengage from one opponent and engage another without provoking an opportunity attack. The new opponent must be within her regular movement rate.

features.name: Hard Eyed
features.description: Valdis has killed before, and will do so again. She scores a critical hit on any 18, 19 or 20 on an attack roll.

features.name: Hate Sunlight
features.description: Valdis despises the cleansing light of the Sun. If she is exposed to direct bright sunlight, she takes 3 (1d6) psychic damage each round.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Valdis makes three attacks: Biting once and making two Claw attacks.

actions.name: Bite
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +5 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 5 (1d6+2) piercing damage and the target must make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or gain 1 Shadow point as the vampire feeds on their blood.

actions.name: Claw
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 9 (2d4+4) slashing damage.

actions.name: Bewilder
actions.description: Valdis can briefly assume the appearance of a beautiful woman. In this form, she can only use her Enthrall ability.

reactions.name: Snake-like Speed (Recharge 5-6)
reactions.description: Valdis is adept at avoiding injury and can use her reaction to halve the attack damage on an attack that she is aware of.

features.name: Leadership
features.description: As a bonus action, Girion can command a nearby Warrior to take his turn immediately after Girion's turn.

features.name: Savage Assault
features.description: When Girion rolls a natural 18 or 19 he may use his bonus action to make a single additional melee attack against the same opponent.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Girion makes three melee attacks.

actions.name: Longsword
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 7 (1d8+3) slashing damage or 8 (1d10+3) piercing damage if used with both hands.

actions.name: Multiattack

actions.name: Black Sword of Mordor
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +8 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 8 (1d8+4) magical slashing damage. The Lieutenant can use his bonus action to add 5 (1d6+2) necrotic damage.

npcs.name: Ruithel
npcs.description: One of the hunters who sets out at the same time as the companions is an Elf-maiden named Ruithel, famed as a huntress and a tracker. She wields one of the treasures of the Woodland Realm, the bow Penbregol, strung with mithril by the Dwarf-smith Gamil Zirak in the depths of time. Ruithel was recently promoted to command the guards who watch the Elf-path and the borders of the Realm, and is eager to prove herself worthy of the office and the bow that comes with it.

npcs.name: Hunald, Spellbound Assassin

features.name: Ambush
features.description: During his first turn, Hunald has Advantage on attack rolls against any creature that hasn't taken a turn.

features.name: Ensorcelled
features.description: Hunald has been dominated by the will of the Nazgûl, and no words will cause him to stray from his mission (reflected in Condition Immunities, above).

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.description: Hunald makes three attacks with either his broadsword or great bow.

actions.name: Broadsword
actions.description: Melee Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. Hit: 8 (1d8+4) slashing damage.

actions.name: Great Bow
actions.description: Ranged Weapon Attack: +6 to hit, range 150/600 ft, one target. Hit: 8 (1d8+4) piercing damage. If Hunald uses one of his arrows from Angmar, it does an additional 7 (2d6) necrotic damage.

npcs.description: Hunald is a Woodman who disappeared in Mirkwood in 2954 while searching for treasure. He is a master bowman, and carries a quiver holding three arrows whose heads were forged in Angmar. He has been dominated by the will of the Nazgûl.

backgrounds.name: Changeling

feature.name: Child of the Woodland Realm
feature.description: Your were raised by the First-born and will likely never be close to your own kin. If you select a Cultural Heirloom as an Open Virtue, you may only select from the Elves of Mirkwood list on page 159 of the Adventures in Middle-earth Player's Guide. You cannot use the Barding heirlooms. When selecting Cultural Virtues you use the Barding list on page 101 of the Player's Guide.

backgrounds.description: You wandered into the enchanted land of the Elves as a young child, and grew up under their care and tutelage. They delighted in your mortal innocence and wonder, and taught you the ways of the Elves. Now, you have returned to the mortal realm, but you remember with fondness the teachings of your foster-parents. You are a child of the twilight, halfway between the starry night of the Elves and the harsh day of the Edain.
